# pulse_ban (Resource)

A manual ban: Pulse refuses connections and requests from the network on its public listeners (and feeds it to the edge firewall and Cloudflare list when those are set up). Destroying the resource lifts the ban.

Pulse refuses to ban loopback, private and link-local ranges, allowlisted networks and Cloudflare's ranges. A temporary ban (`duration_hours` > 0) disappears from Pulse when it expires; the next plan then creates it again. Use `duration_hours = 0` for a permanent ban. Changing any setting forces a new resource (the ban is lifted and placed again). Import with the network in the form Pulse stores it (e.g. `203.0.113.7/32` or `2001:db8:1:2::/64`).

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A permanent ban for a scanner network.
resource "pulse_ban" "scanner" {
  network = "203.0.113.0/24"
  reason  = "Port scans against the public listener"
}

# A single IPv6 address bans its whole /64 (id = "2001:db8:5:6::/64").
resource "pulse_ban" "abuser" {
  network        = "2001:db8:5:6::17"
  reason         = "Credential stuffing"
  duration_hours = 0
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `network` (String) IP address or CIDR to ban (IPv4 or IPv6). Spellings of the same network (e.g. `203.0.113.7` and `203.0.113.7/32`) are treated as the same network. Changing the network forces a new resource.

### Optional

- `duration_hours` (Number) How long the ban lasts, in hours (at most 8760). `0` (the default) means it never expires. Changing it forces a new resource, which starts a new period.
- `reason` (String) Why the network is banned (at most 256 characters). Changing it forces a new resource.

### Read-Only

- `expires_at` (String) When the ban expires (RFC 3339); null for a permanent ban.
- `id` (String) The network as Pulse stores it: a CIDR with the host bits cleared; a single IPv4 address becomes `/32` and a single IPv6 address its `/64` (one host usually controls the whole /64).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import with the network as Pulse stores it (a bare address is also accepted).
terraform import pulse_ban.scanner 203.0.113.0/24
```
